fieldValues.title: May the five spec-corpus source-document sidecars be corrected by hand (srs#1041)?
fieldValues.decision_question: The srs CLI cannot update a source-document sidecar, and the fix for srs#1041 is a one-key change in five sidecars. May those five files be edited by hand, or must the tool gain the capability first?
fieldValues.context:
Problem: all five source-document sidecars in the spec repository write contentPath relative to their own directory, against invariant I-109 (relative to sourceDocumentsPath), so the engine reads each of the five documents as a tombstone and the specification's own repository teaches the form the spec forbids. The fix is one key per file. The CLI has no sidecar-update command: `attachment add` mints a new documentId, which would change identities the sidecars carry today.
Why it matters: the spec repo is the first corpus a third party reads to learn the sidecar format, and this blocks the I-110 check. The repository rule is that data edits go through the CLI and a tool gap is filed and parked, never hand-edited around; sidecars are not records, so the owner may rule an exception.
Options and consequences: (a) Allow a one-off hand edit of the five contentPath values, keeping every other key; fast, and the bytes then read through the engine, but it sets a precedent for hand-editing sidecar metadata. (b) Keep the rule: file an srs-rust issue for a sidecar update command, park srs#1041 until it ships; slower, no precedent. (c) Re-add the five files with `attachment add`; uses the tool, but changes every documentId and loses the original metadata. (d) Do nothing; the five documents stay unreadable through the engine.
Recommendation: (b), unless the owner is content to treat sidecar metadata as hand-editable; then (a) as a recorded, one-off ruling.
Action needed: decide.
Urgency: low to medium; no consumer is blocked beyond the I-110 check.
Answers: SP-01. Issue: the-greenman/srs#1041.
fieldValues.friction: The builder claimed srs#1041, ran the guard (all five still wrong) and then found its plan needs either a hand edit, which repository rules forbid without an owner ruling, or a CLI capability that does not exist. The issue itself names both outcomes.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: (a) One-off hand edit of five contentPath values. (b) File srs-rust sidecar-update command and park srs#1041. (c) Re-add via attachment add, changing documentIds. (d) Do nothing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Every other sidecar key and every documentId unchanged. The engine returns bytes for all five documents. validate-all and check-release-drift green. No precedent set for hand-editing other tool-owned files unless the owner chooses it.
fieldValues.decision_statement: File an srs-rust issue for a sidecar-update command and park srs#1041 until it ships, unless the owner rules a one-off hand edit of the five contentPath values.
fieldValues.rationale: It keeps the CLI-only rule intact and turns the gap into a tracked capability that every corpus can use; the cost is delay on a low-urgency fix.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a sidecar-update command exists, or when a second corpus needs the same fix.
fieldValues.next_steps: Owner rules. If (a): the builder edits the five files, runs both srs gates and opens the PR. If (b): the steward files the srs-rust issue and srs#1041 is parked and blocked by it.
